You may find the information you need in the FAQs about the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz M173 listed below. How can I reduce oscillation when using a wah pedal with the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz? You can engage the buffer switch on the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz to eliminate oscillation issues that sometimes occur when a wah wah pedal is used in conjunction with it. This also helps to brighten the fuzz tone. 0 What should I do if the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz is not powering on? Ensure that the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz is powered by a 9-volt battery or a compatible 9-volt AC adapter. You may need to remove the bottom plate to install or check the battery, or you can use a power supply such as the DC Brick. 0 How can I adjust the amount of fuzz produced by the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz? To adjust the fuzz amount, use the FUZZ knob on the pedal. Rotate it clockwise to increase the fuzz or counterclockwise to decrease it. 0 How do I control the volume of the effect from the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz? Use the VOLUME knob to control the overall effect volume. Turn it clockwise to increase the volume or counterclockwise to decrease it. 0 What should I do if the signal is weak or distorted when using the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz? Check the settings of the VOLUME and FUZZ knobs on the pedal and adjust them accordingly. Additionally, ensure that your cables are properly connected and that the buffer switch is engaged if using a wah pedal that might be affecting the signal. 0 Why is my MXR Classic 108 Fuzz not producing any sound when turned on? Ensure that the power is supplied to the device, either through a 9-volt battery or a compatible AC adapter. Also, check the cables connected to the input and output jacks of the pedal to make sure they are properly connected to your guitar and amplifier. Make sure the footswitch is engaged to turn the effect on. 0 How can I reduce the high-end roll off and oscillation when using the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz with a wah pedal? Engage the BUFFER switch on the MXR Classic 108 Fuzz to eliminate the high-end roll off and oscillation that can occur when a wah pedal is used in front of the distortion pedal. This should also provide a brightening of the fuzz tone. 0 What should I do if the fuzz effect is too intense or too weak on my MXR Classic 108 Fuzz? Adjust the FUZZ knob. Like its larger predecessor, its loaded with the silicon BC-108 transistor for a round and dirty crunch. This Classic 108 Fuzz also has the same no-nonsense control interfacejust crank the Volume and Fuzz controls to your liking and start riffing. Use the Buffer switch on the side to make the fuzz play nice with wah pedals. M296 jimdunlop.com/m296 Page 2 M296 | Classic 108 Fuzz 2 1 OUTPUT knob controls overall effect volume 2 BUFFER switch removes high-end roll off and oscillation caused by some wah pedals 3 FUZZ knob controls fuzz intensity 4 FOOTSWITCH toggles effect on/bypass (blue LED indicates on) 1 3 4 External Controls 2 Page 3 M296 | Classic 108 Fuzz 3 Basic Operation 1 Run a cable from your guitar to the Classic 108 Fuzzs INPUT jack and run another cable from its OUTPUT jack to your amplifier. 2 Start with both knobs at 12 oclock. Turn the effect on by depressing the footswitch. 3 Rotate the FUZZ knob clockwise to increase fuzz intensity or counterclockwise to decrease it. 4 Rotate the VOLUME knob clockwise to increase overall effect volume or counterclockwise to decrease it. 5 Engage the BUFFER switch to eliminate the oscillation that sometimes occurs when a wah pedal is used in front of the Classic 108 Fuzz. You may notice a brightening of the fuzz tone. The Classic 108 Fuzz is powered by the Dunlop ECB003 9-volt adapter or an MXR Brick Series power supply (each sold separately). This pedal cannot be powered by a battery. Guitarists of all styles, from Hendrix devotees to garage rockers and stoner-metal fanatics, will dig the familiar late-Sixties/early-Seventies crunch delivered by the new MXR Classic 108 Fuzz. We've taken the guts of our BC-108 loaded Fuzz Face, placed them in a more pedal-board friendly shape, added the modern conveniences of a battery door, optional AC adapter operation, and true hardwire bypass with LED. The Buffer-Switch removes the classic, Fuzz Face high-end roll off and eliminates the oscillation caused by some wah wahs when placed in front of a Fuzz Face. The Classic 108 Fuzz comes in a heavy-duty Phase 100-sized box with a sweet hammer-tone turquoise finish. - BC108 Fuzz Face circuitry in a pedal-board friendly chassis. - AC adapter or 9-volt battery operation. - True hardwire bypass. - Original Fuzz Face hammer-tone turquoise finish.
